name: Octave
one_liner: Insurance-based talk therapy for individuals, couples and families by video in 22 states, or in person in a few cities.
best_for: Adults with commercial insurance who want weekly talk therapy
Couples or families looking for a therapist who takes insurance
People in its listed states who want video or, in some cities, in-person sessions
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988, or call 911
People with Medicare or Medicaid (not accepted, even for self-pay)
People who need medication or a psychiatrist
short_description: Licensed therapists for individual, couples and family therapy by video in 22 states, billed to commercial insurance or $170–$275 self-pay.
long_description: Octave is a US therapy group practice whose licensed therapists see individuals, couples and families by video and, in some cities, at its clinics. Its FAQ lists 22 states: Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Oregon, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, Washington and Wisconsin, and you must be in your therapist's state during each session. It is in-network with many commercial insurance plans and says most clients pay about $28 a session; self-pay is about $170 to $275 a session (in California $205 for a 45-minute individual session). Octave does not accept Medicare or Medicaid and will not see people with those plans even as self-pay. It offers talk therapy only, with no medication prescribing. No published study of Octave's services was found.
patient_summary: You match with a licensed Octave therapist and meet weekly by video, or in person in cities such as Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York and Philadelphia. Most clients use in-network commercial insurance (Octave says about $28 a session on average); self-pay is about $170 to $275 a session. It does not take Medicare or Medicaid.

pricing.starting_price: Copay with insurance (average about $28/session per Octave); $170–$275/session self-pay
pricing.notes: Commercial insurance only; no Medicare or Medicaid. California self-pay: $205 per 45-minute individual session, $250 per 55-minute couples/family session. Some HSA/FSA cards accepted. Benefits checked before your first session; a cost estimator is on its site.

privacy.notes: Its California privacy notice says third-party advertising and analytics cookies on its website count as a 'sale' under California law; you can opt out, and Global Privacy Control is honored.

faqs.q: How much do Octave therapists get paid?
faqs.a: Octave therapists are W-2 employees with competitive base salaries typically ranging from $70,000-110,000+ depending on experience, license type, and location. Full-time employees receive comprehensive benefits including health insurance, 401k, PTO, and professional development stipends. Octave handles all billing and administrative work.

faqs.q: Where does Octave have clinic locations?
faqs.a: Octave operates premium physical clinic locations in San Francisco, Los Angeles, and New York City. Therapists can see clients in-person at these beautiful, designed spaces or conduct virtual sessions. The hybrid model offers flexibility while maintaining high-quality clinical environments.

faqs.q: What makes Octave different from other therapy platforms?
faqs.a: Octave differentiates itself through its premium physical clinic spaces, hybrid in-person/virtual model, and focus on therapist well-being. As a W-2 employer, Octave provides stability, benefits, and clinical supervision while handling all business aspects. The company emphasizes evidence-based care and measurable outcomes.

Yes, Octave accepts major insurance plans including Aetna, Cigna, and select Blue Cross Blue Shield and UnitedHealthcare plans. Patient copays typically range from $20-60. Self-pay options are also available at $175-250 per session for patients without insurance coverage.

availability.note: 22 states (AZ, CA, CO, CT, FL, GA, IL, MD, MA, MN, NJ, NY, NC, OH, OR, PA, SC, TN, TX, VA, WA, WI); in-person only in select cities. No Medicare or Medicaid.
